lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Assessment preparation: conditional probability and its definition

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A survey table records: group X with 4 successes and 9 failures; group Y with 21 successes and 22 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 3/10, P(B) = 3/10, and P(A and B) = 9/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).

items.prompt: In a group of 21, 8 do activity A, 13 do activity B, and 4 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 3/6 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 47 successes and 16 failures; group Y with 20 successes and 24 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 6/10, P(B) = 9/10, and P(A and B) = 54/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.

items.prompt: In a group of 42, 16 do activity A, 24 do activity B, and 4 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 4/10 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
